subject: Request: Deal Desk sign-off for atypical SLA framework (precedent review)
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Deal Desk sign-off for atypical SLA framework (precedent review)

Team —

MosaicCare is asking for a non-standard SLA and a commercial concession to move their pilot to production. I drafted a proposal with the commercial and technical trade-offs; attaching two docs (SLA-Variance-Proposal-MosaicCare-v1.pdf, MosaicCare-deal-summary-REDWOOD.xlsx). High level:

- Ask: temporary SLA variance for a 90-day pilot, with explicit latency guardrail instead of our usual rigid P99 uptime target.
- Uptime: allow a pilot SLO of 99.70% (standard is 99.95%) for 90 days.
- Latency: P95 <= 280ms; P99 <= 420ms (operational guardrail with exception handling).
- Remedy: tiered service credit capped at 10% of monthly invoice; graded credits only after sustained failures (3+ days below target).
- Commercial: 20% pilot platform discount tied to acceptance of the variance and a monthly observability grade (Console metrics + two sample prompt sets).
- Operational constraints: MosaicCare must enable prefix caching and agree to automatic fallback to a smaller model variant if latency crosses threshold.

Why do we consider this? MosaicCare is a strategic, mid-market vertical customer who will drive referrals in our healthcare channel. They need predictable cost and flexibility during a model-transition period (they're migrating from an on-prem model to our hosted inference).

The risk is precedent. If we allow this as-is it sets a template for future pilots. My recommendation: grant a one-time, time-boxed variance with the following guardrails:

1) Explicit executive sign-off acknowledging the precedent and exposure cap (recommended cap: $40k total credit exposure over the pilot).
2) Legal to add a clause limiting the variance to this single account and forbidding replication without Deal Desk + Exec sign-off.
3) Require MosaicCare to enable data-plane observability (Console access / read-only) and weekly check-ins with CS.

Decision needed by EOD Monday 2027-06-21 to meet MosaicCare procurement timeline. Please reply with: APPROVE / APPROVE w/ CHANGES / DENY and any required edits.

Thanks,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Deal Desk sign-off for atypical SLA framework (precedent review)

Avery / team —

Thanks for the write-up and the attachments. A few legal points we should tighten before sending final approval to execs:

- "One-time" clause: we need explicit language in the addendum that this variance applies only to MosaicCare and does not alter our standard SLA for any other customers.
- Remedy definition: replace open-ended wording with precise triggers (e.g., "service credit applies when rolling 30-day uptime < 99.70% and at least one incident has impacted 50%+ of requests per day"). This prevents small noisy blips from creating credit exposure.
- Cap mechanics: the proposed $40k cap should be expressed as a percentage of monthly bill in the contract (e.g., cap = min($40k, 10% of monthly invoice)) so the exposure scales predictably.
- Audit and security: require MosaicCare to complete our standard security questionnaire and provide recent SOC2 report; attach as contract precondition.

Also recommend we add a rollback clause: if during the pilot we observe systemic degradation across our region, Redwood reserves the right to revert MosaicCare to the standard SLA or suspend the pilot with 7 days' notice.

If we incorporate the above edits, I'm comfortable escalating for Sean's executive sign-off.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Folks —

I've reviewed the thread and attachments. Given MosaicCare's strategic potential and the mitigations Jonas proposed, I will provide conditional executive authorization to proceed with the variance as described, subject to the following firm constraints:

1) Time-box: limited to a single 90-calendar-day pilot. No automatic extension.
2) Exposure cap: total service-credit liability limited to min($40,000, 10% of the monthly invoice) across the pilot. This is final.
3) Legal edits: Jonas to implement the "one-time" clause, precise remedy triggers, and a rollback clause. No variance to be treated as precedent in our template library without my explicit re-authorization.
4) Security & compliance: MosaicCare must provide SOC2 report and complete the security questionnaire prior to production traffic.
5) Observability gating: CS must grant read-only Console access and provide the weekly dashboard. CS to confirm onboarding KPI sign-off before any discount is applied.
6) Billing control: Finance to withhold the 20% discount until CS confirms the onboarding checklist; discount applied retroactively only if onboarding criteria are met.

Jonas/Marissa — please incorporate the wording, generate the addendum (DocuSign link preferred), and route back to me for record. Avery — align the MosaicCare procurement timelines with these conditions and confirm acceptance.

Approved as: APPROVE w/ CONDITIONS (see above).

Sean Gallagher
VP, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference
